audit.summary: The actual pointwise conclusion of Proposition 5 fails after constant-field extension; Theorem 22 fails for a punctured quadratic Artin–Schreier sheaf. Lemma 9 needs analytic and positive-dimensional scope, and zero-weight conjugation is not choice independent.
limitations: Actual pointwise factor does not follow from a constant-field extension — Counterevidence: The nonconstant double cover trivializes the system; the almost local comparison survives because both eigenvalues become 1 after squaring. At Frobenius -1 no conjugating g enters the trivial torus, so the earlier conditional statement is not separately contradicted.

Elementary finite generic monodromy does not ensure Fourier weight1 realization — Counterevidence: Specific pure middle-extension Katz and Bültel examples are not thereby refuted. The actual Katz definition 7.3.7 includes the missing middle-extension condition.

Density lemma omits analyticity and positive-dimensional scope — Counterevidence: For positive-dimensional S, the subset actually used in the proof of 9(2) is analytic. Positive upper density still gives an open generated subgroup by Haar measure. The main local-global questions for Spec k are trivial and can be treated separately.

Conjugating torus maps have Weyl ambiguity — Counterevidence: A chosen conjugating element still induces a natural isomorphism in representations. The weaker up-to-natural-isomorphism assertion and the ghost dimension/isomorphism class are not refuted. The article's own large-monodromy example supplies the corresponding adjoint situation; its external existence input was not independently re-proved.

proposition.claim:
After extending only k, the rank dim(V^{barT}) ghost is an actual submodule of every semisimplified closed fiber.

Odd q; S=G_m over F_q; for all ell not equal to p, use the sign sheaf of u -> u^2. Rank one, rational compatible and pure of weight zero. Geometric monodromy is mu_2, with trivial maximal torus.

Every elementary constructible sheaf with finite generic monodromy has Fourier transform appearing as direct factor of an abelian R1 on some nonempty open.

k=F_3, ell=2, nontrivial additive character psi into Qbar_2*. Let j:G_m -> A^1, i:{0} -> A^1, L=L_psi(t^2), F=j_!j^*L. The generic rank is one and monodromy has order three.

The zero-density/empty-interior equivalence is asserted for every closed conjugacy-invariant set. The density-one topological and Zariski conclusions are stated in a setup that also allows dimension zero.

Part A: S=A^1 over F_3, ell=2, rho(F_s)=u(n_s) in u(Z_2). Part B: S=Spec F_3 with the same arithmetic unipotent representation.

A conjugating element with T'=gTg^(-1) is unique modulo right multiplication by T, and hence the map on the zero-weight space is independent of g.

Connected semisimple SL_2, diagonal torus T and adjoint representation sl_2. No pointwise identification of the two tori is fixed in the claimed uniqueness statement.

repair.content:
State actual comparison on a suitable finite étale cover, or establish almost comparison on the original base with an explicit descent argument.

Require the appropriate pure middle-extension hypothesis, or formulate a realization statement for a suitable weight-one quotient.

Assume dim S>0 in the density machinery. Require closed analytic Phi in the empty-interior equivalence, or use the general Haar-measure bounds.

Remove uniqueness, retain the normalizer/Weyl ambiguity, and arrange compatible choices at the pro-reductive level.
